column1: # above it, reviewed like a waiver (ADR 006). High-risk findings fail the nightly run either way.
# Pages and the app shell are sent "no-cache" on purpose: kiosks must pick up a new release at
# once. Every response with patient or account data is "no-store" (checked by prod_smoke.py).
# The flagged files are the build's content-hashed /assets (public code and styles, no data),
# cached for 30 days as immutable; a new release has new file names.
# Informational: the scanner noting a single-page application.
# Known and accepted for now: React style attributes and the splash <style> need it (see
# infra/web/security-headers.conf). Scripts stay 'self' only, which is what stops injection.
# The API scan also requests the web app's own paths: unknown paths return the single-page
# app (text/html) and static files their own types (JavaScript, fonts, CSS). API answers are
# JSON, CSV or PDF as documented; nginx's own errors are problem JSON (nginx.tls.conf).
